subject: business-studies
title: ZIMSEC O-Level Business Enterprise and Skills

officialDocument.title: Business Enterprise Skills Syllabus, Forms 1 - 4, 2015 - 2022 (Ministry of Primary and Secondary Education, Curriculum Development and Technical Services), examined by ZIMSEC at O Level
officialDocument.publisher: Ministry of Primary and Secondary Education (Curriculum Development and Technical Services) / Zimbabwe School Examinations Council (ZIMSEC)

sourceNote: Topic names and the numbers 7.1 to 7.8 are transcribed from the scope and sequence (7.0) of the Ministry's Business Enterprise Skills Syllabus Forms 1 - 4 (2015 - 2022); the sub-topics are the scope-and-sequence items for Forms 1 to 4, and the competency matrix (8.1 to 8.4) supplied their content. Sub-topic codes (7.1.1, ...) and objective codes are ours, not the board's; where the same item recurs in several forms, or two short items belong together, they are grouped into one sub-topic and the forms are given in its description. Learning-objective statements are our own paraphrase; no syllabus text is reproduced.
notes: Source (read 2026-10-08): the Mashonaland West provincial education office's copy of the Ministry document, file 'Business Enterprise and Skills.pdf' (http://www.mopsemashwest.gov.zw/files/Business%20Enterprise%20and%20Skills.pdf; the site's https certificate has expired, so the https URL recorded here may not load), read through a text rendering. The document's own title is 'Business Enterprise Skills' (Forms 1 - 4, 2015 - 2022); the catalogue name 'Business Enterprise and Skills' is kept. The scope-and-sequence and competency-matrix tables are partly scrambled in the rendering; check every heading and objective against a clean copy from ZIMSEC and record the exact document URL.
Subject code: not printed in the syllabus document; confirm the ZIMSEC code for this subject (code left null).

Version dates: assumed first examined in November 2018 (effectiveFrom 2018-01-01), as for the other 2015-2022 files. Under the Heritage-Based Curriculum (2024-2030) new syllabi were issued; confirm which syllabus the November 2026 and later O-Level examinations in this subject use, set effectiveTo, and create a new version file when a new syllabus replaces this one.

Assessment (9.0) as read: continuous assessment 40% (theory tests 6%, assignments 8%, practical projects 26%, including at least two enterprise projects: one in Forms 1-2 and one in Forms 3-4) and a summative examination 60%: Paper 1, structured short questions (six questions, 1 hour 45 minutes, 100 marks, 30%); Paper 2, case study and essays (2 hours 15 minutes, 100 marks, 30%): Section A, one case study worth 40 marks; Section B, three essays from a choice of six, worth 60 marks. The marks of each Paper 1 question are not stated. Whether calculators are allowed is not stated (calculatorAllowed left out).

Specification grid (9.4) as read: Paper 1 and Paper 2 weighted 30% each across knowledge with understanding, application, analysis and evaluation; some cells could not be read reliably in the rendering.

Uncertain placements: the scope and sequence lists 'Organisational structure' and 'Financial and non-financial methods of motivation' in the Form 4 column of People in business enterprises, but the text rendering shows no Form 4 competency-matrix section for that topic (financial and non-financial methods appear in the Form 2 matrix). 'Cash budgets' appears in both the Form 2 and Form 3 columns. 'Business size' appears in Forms 2, 3 and 4. Confirm against a clean copy.

Practical projects (an enterprise project in Forms 1-2 and another in Forms 3-4) and the mini-enterprise activities are continuous assessment: the platform supports them only with planning guidance, not assessment.

The family also serves ZIMSEC Commerce and Cambridge IGCSE Business: concepts covered only by those syllabi (for example banking services in depth, insurance, trade documents, recruitment and the business cycle) are not part of this syllabus.
overview: ZIMSEC O-Level Business Enterprise and Skills (Forms 1-4) develops enterprising skills through eight topics: the business enterprise and the enterpriser, the enterprising environment, setting up a new enterprise, business planning, enterprise finance and securing investors (including financial statements, cash budgets, costs and break-even), people in business enterprises, markets and marketing, and operations management.
assessmentOverview: Continuous assessment (theory tests, assignments and two enterprise projects) carries 40%. The examination carries 60%: Paper 1 has six structured short questions (1 hour 45 minutes, 100 marks, 30%) and Paper 2 (2 hours 15 minutes, 100 marks, 30%) has one compulsory case study worth 40 marks in Section A and three essays chosen from six, worth 60 marks, in Section B.

components.name: Paper 1: Structured short questions
components.description: Six compulsory structured questions on the whole syllabus.

components.name: Paper 2: Case study and essays
components.description: Section A (40 marks): one compulsory case study. Section B (60 marks): three essays chosen from six.

children.name: Enterprising; skills and personal attributes of an enterpriser
children.description: Form 1: enterprising, enterpriser and enterprise; skills and attributes; benefits and drawbacks of enterprising.

objectives.text: Explain the concept of enterprising.
Identify and explain the skills and personal attributes needed to run an enterprise.
Identify the benefits and drawbacks of enterprising.

children.name: The role of an enterpriser; drivers towards enterprising
children.description: Form 2 (role of the enterpriser) and Form 3 (drivers towards enterprising).

objectives.text: Explain the role of an enterpriser in an enterprise.
Explain and evaluate the drivers towards enterprising.

children.name: Internal and external stakeholders
children.description: Form 1.

objectives.text: Distinguish between internal and external stakeholders.
Explain the role of each stakeholder.

children.name: Resources and capabilities
children.description: Form 1 (need for resources and capabilities) and Form 2 (acquisition, ownership and sustainable use of resources).

objectives.text: Differentiate resources from capabilities and explain why they are analysed.
Identify tangible and intangible resources needed in an enterprise.
Identify ways of acquiring resources and analyse forms of resource ownership.
Explain ways of using resources sustainably and why this matters.

children.name: Internal and external environment; business constraints
children.description: Form 2 (internal and external environment, SWOT analysis) and Form 3 (economic, ecological, social and legal constraints).

objectives.text: Describe the internal and external environmental factors that affect an enterprise.
Carry out a SWOT analysis of an enterprise.
Explain business constraints and analyse their effects.

children.name: Business opportunities and risks
children.description: Form 4.

objectives.text: Investigate how business opportunities arise.
Identify the risks associated with business enterprises and assess their likelihood and impact.

children.name: Purpose of business enterprises
children.description: Form 1: employment creation, infrastructure development and other purposes.

objectives.text: Explain the purposes of business enterprises.

children.name: Unincorporated business enterprises; setting up a sole proprietorship or partnership
children.description: Form 1 (forms of unincorporated enterprise) and Form 2 (setting one up).

objectives.text: Identify and describe the forms of unincorporated business enterprise.
Explain the advantages and disadvantages of unincorporated business enterprises.
Describe the process of setting up a sole proprietorship or partnership.

children.name: Incorporated business enterprises
children.description: Form 2: limited companies.

objectives.text: Explain the features of incorporated business enterprises.
Analyse the benefits and limitations of different incorporated enterprises.

children.name: Business ethics
children.description: Form 2.

objectives.text: Explain issues concerning business ethics.
Evaluate the importance of being ethical in business and apply ethics in projects.

children.name: Causes of business failure
children.description: Form 2.

objectives.text: Discuss why some businesses fail.
Suggest solutions to the causes of business failure.

children.name: Forms of business enterprises
children.description: Form 3: public corporations, joint ventures and franchises.

objectives.text: Describe the features of public corporations, joint ventures and franchises.
Analyse the advantages and disadvantages of each form and compare them.

children.name: Assistance to enterprise start-ups
children.description: Form 3.

objectives.text: Justify why new business enterprises need support.
Identify ways in which start-ups are supported.

children.name: Business size
children.description: Form 3 (small and large businesses) and Form 4 (measuring size; small to medium enterprises and government assistance to them).

objectives.text: Explain why some enterprises grow and others remain small.
Discuss the advantages and disadvantages of small and large enterprises.
Evaluate methods of measuring business size.
Discuss the role of small to medium enterprises in the economy and identify government assistance to them.

children.name: Business growth
children.description: Form 2 (factors influencing growth) and Form 4 (methods and effects of growth).

objectives.text: Describe factors influencing business growth.
Identify and evaluate methods of business growth.
Assess the effects of business growth.

children.name: Risk, ownership and limited liability; formation of a business enterprise
children.description: Form 4: risks of forming an enterprise, corporate legal personality and limited liability, documents required.

objectives.text: Explain the risks of forming a new business enterprise.
Explain corporate legal personality and limited liability and evaluate the importance of limited liability.
Explain the contents of the documents required to form a business enterprise.

children.name: Purpose of business planning; the business plan
children.description: Form 1 (purpose, a mini business plan) and Form 3 (components of a business plan, developing a plan).

objectives.text: Explain business planning and the purpose and importance of a business plan.
Explain the components of a business plan.
Develop a business plan.

children.name: Business objectives
children.description: Form 1.

objectives.text: Identify different business objectives.

children.name: Business planning process; implementation of a business plan
children.description: Form 2 (planning process) and Form 4 (implementation).

objectives.text: Describe the business planning process and the importance of each step.
Implement a business plan on a selected project and manage it.

children.name: The need for finance
children.description: Form 1: the need for finance; investment and saving.

objectives.text: Explain the need for finance in an enterprise.
Explain investment and saving.

children.name: Sources of finance
children.description: Form 1.

objectives.text: Identify sources of finance and differentiate internal from external sources.
Explain the advantages and disadvantages of various sources of finance.
Identify factors to consider when choosing a source of finance.

children.name: Financial statements
children.description: Forms 2 and 3: the income statement and the statement of financial position.

objectives.text: Explain the importance of keeping accurate financial records.
Prepare an income statement.
Draw up a statement of financial position.

children.name: Cash budgets
children.description: Forms 2 and 3.

objectives.text: Describe a cash budget and identify cash inflows and outflows.
Prepare a simple cash budget and use it on a project.

children.name: Working capital
children.description: Form 3.

objectives.text: Explain the meaning of working capital and identify the components of the working capital cycle.
Discuss the importance of managing working capital and explain ways of managing it.

children.name: Financial institutions
children.description: Form 3: merchant banks, commercial banks, discount houses and others.

objectives.text: Identify different types of financial institution.
Explain the functions of different financial institutions.

children.name: Business costs
children.description: Form 4: fixed, variable, direct and indirect costs.

objectives.text: Classify business costs.

children.name: Break-even analysis
children.description: Form 4: break-even point, profit and loss regions and margin of safety.

objectives.text: Explain break-even analysis and discuss its importance.
Construct a break-even chart.
Calculate the break-even point and the margin of safety for a business venture.

children.name: Budgeting and budgets
children.description: Form 4: cash, sales, production and purchases budgets.

objectives.text: Explain budgeting and budgets and identify types of budget.
Prepare a budget for an enterprise and explain the importance of budgeting.

children.name: Securing investors
children.description: Form 4.

objectives.text: Explain different ways of attracting investors.

children.name: Functions of managers
children.description: Form 2: planning, leading, organising and controlling.

objectives.text: Explain the functions of managers in a business.

children.name: Motivating employees; financial and non-financial methods of motivation
children.description: Form 2 (and Form 4 in the scope and sequence).

objectives.text: Explain the benefits of motivated employees.
Identify financial and non-financial methods of motivating employees.
Investigate how local employees are motivated.

children.name: Motivation theories
children.description: Form 3: Maslow, Taylor, Herzberg and McGregor.

objectives.text: Identify and discuss the theories of motivation.
Assess how well motivation theories apply to different enterprises.

children.name: Leadership
children.description: Form 3: qualities of a leader and leadership styles.

objectives.text: Explain leadership and identify the qualities of a good leader.
Discuss different leadership styles.

children.name: Business communication
children.description: Form 3: importance, methods and media of communication and the impact of ICTs.

objectives.text: Explain business communication and analyse its importance.
Evaluate methods of communication and justify the choice of method and medium in given circumstances.
Assess the impact of ICTs on business communication.

children.name: Organisational structure
children.description: Form 4 (listed in the scope and sequence; the text rendering shows no competency-matrix section for it).

objectives.text: Describe and interpret the organisational structure of an enterprise.

children.name: The need for marketing
children.description: Form 1: market, product, demand and supply; the importance of marketing.

objectives.text: Explain the meaning of market, product, demand and supply.
Discuss the importance of marketing to business enterprises.
Explain the relationship between demand and supply.

children.name: Types of markets
children.description: Form 2: physical and virtual, local, regional and global markets; foreign markets.

objectives.text: Identify and explain types of markets and the features of physical and virtual markets.
Discuss the advantages and disadvantages of physical and virtual markets.
Evaluate the benefits and challenges of foreign markets and suggest ways of reducing the challenges.

children.name: Marketing research
children.description: Form 3: types and sources of data, sampling, data collection tools, presentation and analysis.

objectives.text: Explain marketing research and identify types and sources of research data.
Apply sampling methods and design data collection tools.
Present research data in tables, graphs and charts and interpret it.

children.name: Market segmentation
children.description: Form 3.

objectives.text: Discuss factors to consider when segmenting a market and the reasons for segmentation.
Segment a market.

children.name: Demand forecasting
children.description: Form 3.

objectives.text: Explain the importance of demand forecasting.
Identify methods of demand forecasting.

children.name: Economic integration
children.description: Form 4: regional economic integration such as SADC, COMESA and ECOWAS.

objectives.text: Explain the concept of economic integration and describe the aims of different economic blocs.
Explain the advantages and disadvantages of economic integration.

children.name: Marketing mix
children.description: Form 4: product (development, life cycle, packaging, branding), price, place and promotion.

objectives.text: Identify and explain the marketing mix variables.
Evaluate the impact of the marketing mix variables on marketing.
Suggest appropriate pricing, product, distribution and promotion strategies for a given market.

children.name: Nature of production
children.description: Form 1: means of production, stages of production and the production function.

objectives.text: Identify the means and the stages of production.
Explain and illustrate the production function.

children.name: Location of production
children.description: Form 1: location and relocation factors.

objectives.text: Identify factors influencing the location of a business unit.
Discuss factors that lead to the relocation of a business.

children.name: Value addition
children.description: Form 2.

objectives.text: Explain value addition, ways of adding value and why it is important.
Create a product using locally available inputs.

children.name: Transport
children.description: Form 2: importance, modes and choice of transport.

objectives.text: Explain the importance of transport and identify the modes of transport.
Describe the strengths and weaknesses of the different modes.
Explain the factors influencing the choice of mode of transport.

children.name: Purchasing; inventory management
children.description: Form 3: the purchasing function and cycle, e-purchasing, types of inventory and the costs and benefits of holding inventory.

objectives.text: Explain the importance of the purchasing function and identify the five rights of purchasing.
Explain the stages of the purchasing cycle and the role of e-purchasing.
Describe inventory management and the advantages and disadvantages of holding inventory.

children.name: Warehousing
children.description: Form 4: the role, types and location of warehouses.

objectives.text: Describe the role of warehousing.
State different types of warehouse and explain their functions.
Explain factors to consider when locating a warehouse.

children.name: Quality management
children.description: Form 4: total quality management, quality circles and just-in-time.

objectives.text: Analyse the importance of producing quality products.
Explain ways of assuring quality.

children.name: ICTs in operations management
children.description: Form 4: bar codes, radio frequency identification, computer-aided design and online billing.

objectives.text: Evaluate the impact of ICTs in operations management.
Recommend appropriate ICT tools for given circumstances.
